current_games.title: Kentucky Route Zero
current_games.why: Shares NORCO's magical-realist Southern melancholy and slow, poetic vignettes.

current_games.title: Gone Home
current_games.why: Like What Remains of Edith Finch, it's a house-as-memoir told through objects and rooms, but grounded in one family's ordinary secrets rather than fable.

current_games.title: Virginia
current_games.why: Wordless, cinematic storytelling in the Edith Finch and Before Your Eyes mold.

current_games.title: Mutazione
current_games.why: A soap-opera adventure with the character-driven warmth Roadwarden fans tend to love.

current_games.title: Signalis
current_games.why: A retro top-down homage to classic Resident Evil with Silent Hill dread.

current_games.title: The Evil Within 2
current_games.why: Shinji Mikami's follow-up to the RE4 lineage — a natural next stop after Resident Evil Village.

current_games.title: SOMA
current_games.why: Underwater existential horror with the atmospheric menace of Alien: Isolation.

current_games.title: Amnesia: The Bunker
current_games.why: Since you loved Alien: Isolation, this offers the same unscripted stalker AI and scarcity-driven dread, with one persistent monster hunting you through a semi-open WWI bunker.

current_games.title: Ion Fury
current_games.why: A step sideways from DUSK's occult minimalism into dense, secret-packed Build-engine city levels, with the same chunky arsenal that makes Turbo Overkill fun.

current_games.title: AMID EVIL
current_games.why: Heretic-inspired arcane arenas for anyone who devoured DOOM Eternal's combat loop.

current_games.title: Prodeus
current_games.why: Modern-feeling retro FPS with the meaty weapon feedback of DOOM and Turbo Overkill.

current_games.title: ULTRAKILL
current_games.why: Style-meter carnage that matches the frantic momentum of Turbo Overkill.

current_games.title: Dragon's Dogma 2
current_games.why: A weird, systemic fantasy world for Elden Ring and Skyrim wanderers.

current_games.title: Gothic II
current_games.why: Grounded, hostile medieval RPG that pairs beautifully with Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

current_games.title: Outward
current_games.why: Survival-flavoured RPG travel that echoes The Long Dark meeting Skyrim.

current_games.title: ELEX II
current_games.why: A rough-edged post-apoc RPG with the faction politics Witcher 3 fans enjoy.

current_games.title: Gloomwood
current_games.why: A direct spiritual successor to Thief: The Dark Project — light-and-shadow sneaking, sword and blackjack, and a Victorian horror city you learn by listening.

current_games.title: Deus Ex: The Nameless Mod
current_games.why: Since you loved Deus Ex, this sprawling fan-made total conversion delivers the same multi-path hubs, hacking and stealth-or-guns freedom in a wholly new story.

current_games.title: Invisible, Inc.
current_games.why: Broadens on Shadow Tactics' squad stealth by making it turn-based and procedural, so each espionage run is improvised rather than a memorized puzzle.

current_games.title: Styx: Shards of Darkness
current_games.why: Pure stealth-first level design for anyone who savours MGSV's quiet approaches.

current_games.title: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
current_games.why: From the Titanfall 2 studio, it blends Arkham-style combat rhythm with Uncharted-flavoured climbing and a strong linear-cinematic spine.

current_games.title: A Plague Tale: Innocence
current_games.why: Like Uncharted 4, it's a tightly directed, character-driven set-piece journey, and its bleak sibling-survival tone echoes your love of Little Nightmares II.

current_games.title: Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition
current_games.why: Broadens the Mad Max open-world vehicular chaos into an undercover crime story, hitting the same beat as your love for Mafia: Definitive Edition.

current_games.title: Sifu
current_games.why: Choreographed brawling with the stylish momentum God of War and Ghost of Tsushima fans crave.

history.title: Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun
